claims.text: Adding controlled amounts of carbon and nitrogen during spark plasma sintering of WNbMoTa will promote in situ formation of ultrafine carbide/nitride dispersoids.
The carbon/nitrogen-derived precipitates will be nanoscale and uniformly distributed within the BCC WNbMoTa matrix.
The nano-dispersoids will impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion will precipitation-strengthen the alloy.
The nano-dispersoids will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Defect-sink behavior will enhance mechanical performance under irradiation.
Introducing the nano-dispersoids will not compromise the high-temperature phase stability of WNbMoTa.
The carbon/nitrogen-modified alloy will have greater yield strength than undoped WNbMoTa.
The carbon/nitrogen-modified alloy will have greater hardness than undoped WNbMoTa.
The nano-dispersoids will remain stable during exposure at temperatures of at least 1000 °C.
The nano-dispersoids will remain stable during irradiation exposure.
WNbMoTa produced without deliberate carbon or nitrogen additions lacks the proposed beneficial nano-dispersoids.
Undoped WNbMoTa has lower strength than the proposed carbon/nitrogen-modified material.
Undoped WNbMoTa has poorer irradiation-defect management than the proposed modified material.
A short anneal at approximately 1200–1300 °C after spark plasma sintering will be compatible with formation or retention of the desired nanoscale precipitate population.
A uniform nanoscale precipitate distribution is necessary for the proposed benefits.
Extensive coarsening or clustering during thermal or irradiation exposure could reduce the strengthening effect.
